generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, reflection becomes a habit across a module rather than a task at the end. After a lab report or an essay on a study, a short honest look back - what did I grasp, what did I rush - with one change carried into the next piece is worth more than a long write-up written only when asked.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students get the same note on a report: the analysis was thin. One reads it and moves on. The other looks back honestly, sees they skimmed the method, and plans to read it closely next time. Over the term their reports sharpen, because reflection became a practice rather than a one-off.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, reflection works best as a continuing practice. You look back honestly after each piece, change one thing, and carry it into the next study, report or essay.

check.body: A psychology student does well in one lab report, reads the feedback, and uses it to plan the next report, which comes back stronger. Which part of the learning, assessment and feedback cycle did using that feedback feed back into?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.
